slides.title: AI vs. AI
slides.subtitle: Building Resilient Enterprises in the Age of Autonomous Threats

slides.name: DINIS CRUZ
slides.role:
GenAI Entrepreneur & Former CISO
Akeia.ai / The Cyber Boardroom / MyFeeds.ai
slides.notes: Brief introduction - ex-CISO background, now building AI security tools. Set the tone: this talk challenges conventional AI security narrative.

slides.title: THE PERFECT STORM
slides.subtitle: Why This Moment Is Different
slides.notes: Transition: Set up the convergence of forces creating unprecedented risk

slides.title: SECURITY'S FOUR PILLARS - ALL BROKEN

items.label: Engineering & Technology
items.text: We know how to build secure systems - we don't do it at scale

items.label: Business Processes
items.text: Security is an afterthought, not embedded in decisions

items.label: Funding & Focus
items.text: NFRs chronically underfunded - features always win

items.label: Risk Management
items.text: Spreadsheets and heat maps disconnected from technical reality

slides.insight: Systems are insecure not because engineers are stupid, but because the ENVIRONMENT forces corner-cutting. All four pillars must be aligned.
slides.notes: Key insight: Systems are insecure not because engineers are stupid, but because the ENVIRONMENT forces corner-cutting. All four pillars must be aligned for security to work.

slides.title: WE'VE BEEN GETTING AWAY WITH IT

items.label: AWS
items.text: Timing bug wiped out a global database

items.label: Azure
items.text: Config inconsistency silently propagated, then 'detonated' worldwide

items.label: Cloudflare
items.text: Routine config change crashed bot defense, halted traffic

items.label: CrowdStrike
items.text: 8.5 million Windows systems bricked by a faulty update

slides.insight: These weren't sophisticated attacks - they were minor glitches that cascaded. Now imagine if they were deliberate, coordinated attacks.
slides.notes: The inefficiencies and limitations of legacy systems acted as a safety buffer. That buffer is disappearing as we automate and interconnect everything.

slides.title: THE NEW INSIDERS
slides.subtitle: Autonomous Agents as Threat Actors
slides.notes: Transition: Reframe the threat model - it's not just external attackers. The biggest risks may come from within.

slides.title: THREE CATEGORIES OF AI-DRIVEN THREATS

items.label: Malicious AI Agents
items.text: Fully autonomous malware that learns, adapts, and persists

items.label: Compromised Benign Agents
items.text: Your AI bots hijacked via prompt injection - operating with legitimate access, now working for the adversary

items.label: Unintentionally Harmful Agents
items.text: The paperclip maximizer scenario - dangerously efficient in ways we didn't anticipate

slides.insight: Prompt injection remains unsolved - any AI taking untrusted input can be subverted.
slides.notes: Prompt injection remains unsolved - any AI taking untrusted input can be subverted. We're essentially never had a malicious insider with near-infinite patience and the ability to instantly devise new approaches.

slides.title: HUMAN INSIDERS VS. AI AGENTS

items: Natural limitations on skill and time
No moral compass unless explicitly constrained

slides.insight: We've never had a malicious insider that can instantly devise new approaches when initial attempts fail. AI doesn't give up - it gets creative.
slides.notes: Key insight: We've never had a malicious insider that can instantly devise new approaches when initial attempts fail. AI doesn't give up - it gets creative.

slides.title: WHY ENTERPRISES AREN'T READY
slides.subtitle: Fragile by Design
slides.notes: Transition: The uncomfortable truth about our infrastructure

slides.title: FRAGILE BY DEFAULT

children: ~40% of IT asset value is technical debt (McKinsey)
Systems running 'hot' with minimal safety margins
Internet = circular dependency machine
Identity, DNS, cloud, CDN - one failure cascades globally
Only ~54% have documented DR plans - fewer actually test them
Average breach detection: 9 months of dwell time
Code has Git. Databases? Configs? Often nothing.
If an AI corrupts records, can you rewind?

slides.notes: You can't protect what you don't understand. You can't recover what you haven't practiced. If you don't know what an AI agent did last week, how do you 'undo' it?

slides.title: THE DEFENDER'S EDGE
slides.subtitle: AI as Force Multiplier, Not Black Box
slides.notes: Transition: Here's where we flip the script. This is the core message.

slides.title: ATTACKERS ALWAYS MAKE MISTAKES

children: You cannot patch everything, eliminate every gap
And you don't have to
Unusual logins, wrong processes, odd data movement
Attackers lack perfect insider knowledge - they wander, they probe
Before they reach the crown jewels
Whether it's an external attacker OR your own AI spiraling

slides.notes: This reframes the entire game. Perfect prevention is impossible AND unnecessary. Detection and response are the asymmetric advantage. Real breaches require MANY failures - one click shouldn't mean total collapse.

slides.title: SECURITY'S ASYMMETRIC ADVANTAGE

children: Access to every system, every data flow
One of few functions focused on business SURVIVAL, not narrow objectives
You define the baseline - attackers must deviate from it
The moment something acts outside normal, you catch it
Attackers wander chasing dead ends, making noise
You know the terrain - use it

slides.notes: Defenders think in lists, attackers think in graphs. As long as this is true, attackers win. We need to arm defenders with graphs - and the AI to make sense of them.

slides.title: THE MECHANISM: KNOWLEDGE GRAPHS

content.text: Build a Digital Twin of Your Enterprise
children: Systems, data flows, identities, dependencies - all connected
Not static docs - a living, queryable model
Each team's data model connects to the whole
Query: 'What breaks if System X goes down?' - instant answer

content.text: AI Builds and Maintains the Graph
children: LLMs digest docs, configs, logs into structure
Humans make decisions, AI updates the map continuously

slides.notes: This is the HOW of 'understanding your enterprise'. Not magic - graphs + AI. Use GenAI to BUILD the knowledge, but deterministic systems for real-time enforcement. The graph is your situational awareness.

slides.title: RADICAL SIMPLIFICATION
slides.subtitle: The Answer Isn't More Complexity
slides.notes: Transition: Counter-intuitive but essential. Every agent you add becomes part of your attack surface.

slides.title: ASSUME COMPROMISE, CONTAIN BLAST RADIUS

children: Crown-jewel systems walled off with strict controls
One-way isolation for legacy components that can't be fixed
Parts may fail, but they fail SAFELY
No cascade into total enterprise collapse

content.text: Hardened Boundaries Around What Can't Be Fixed
children: API throttles for fragile older systems
Circuit breakers that halt abnormal transactions automatically

slides.notes: The race isn't to deploy GenAI defenses faster - every agent you add to mission-critical systems becomes part of your attack surface. Simplify first.

slides.title: VERSION CONTROL EVERYTHING

content.text: Code Has Git. What About Data?
children: If an AI corrupts your database, can you rewind?
Most orgs: No version history, no audit trail, no rollback
Every change recorded and reversible
Tampering becomes evident because history can't be rewritten
Simpler architecture = smaller attack surface
Standard backup/versioning tools work out of the box

slides.notes: SBOMs act like Git commits for software. Extend that concept to ALL enterprise data. If you can't surgically undo what a malicious process did, you have no resilience.

slides.title: IDENTITY GRAPHS: LEAST PRIVILEGE AT SCALE

children: Users, services, AI agents - all in one graph
Query: 'If this account is compromised, what can it reach?'
Privileges that EXPIRE, not persist
Admin rights only when explicitly unlocked, auto-revoke after
One compromised account ≠ full breach
Attacker hits walls immediately - can't pivot everywhere

slides.notes: Identity is the new perimeter. Traditional over-provisioning worked when attacks were slow. With AI-speed attacks, only graph-based, automated IAM keeps up. Zero Trust isn't a product - it's this architecture.

slides.title: FUND NFRs AT UNPRECEDENTED SCALE
content: Comprehensive backup and restore drills - actually TEST them
Chaos engineering beyond normal peaks - AI doesn't respect office hours
Consolidate overly complex workflows - fewer moving parts = fewer failure points
Demand robustness from vendors - the market doesn't currently punish fragility
slides.notes: Non-functional requirements: scalability, fault tolerance, observability, recoverability. If it isn't measured or required in contracts, it doesn't get done. Time to change that.

slides.title: ENABLING INNOVATION
slides.subtitle: Security as Enabler, Not Gatekeeper
slides.notes: Transition: Don't become the Department of No. The horse has bolted.

slides.title: VIBE CODING: THE NEW SPREADSHEETS

content.text: Creating Software Is Now Trivially Easy
children: Non-engineers building apps via AI prompts
If the software doesn't exist, they will it into existence over coffee

content.text: Same Pattern as Excel - On Steroids
children: Solves immediate problem brilliantly
Becomes mission-critical overnight
Zero security, testing, or governance built in
Employees pasting sensitive data into ChatGPT daily
Department-level AI tools running under IT's radar

slides.notes: Just like spreadsheets couldn't be banned, vibe coding won't be stopped. The question isn't IF but HOW you govern it. Security teams that try to block this become irrelevant.

slides.title: DON'T BECOME THE DEPARTMENT OF 'NO'

children: Employees will use AI regardless of policy
Shadow-IT AI is far worse than governed AI
Provide vetted platforms and clear guidelines
Build safe internal AI services before they run to ChatGPT
Pair business 'vibe coders' with engineering buddies
When a prototype gets traction, help industrialize it safely

slides.notes: We did this for cloud - shifted from 'no cloud' to 'here's a secure cloud framework'. Time to do it again for GenAI. Position security as the adults who make the cool new toy safe for everyone.

slides.title: THE PATH FORWARD
slides.subtitle: From Reactive Firefighting to Proactive Containment
slides.notes: Transition: Wrap up with clear call to action

slides.title: CALL TO ACTION

children: Knowledge graphs of your enterprise - don't wait for a crisis
Catch the 5-10 mistakes attackers will make
Every agent you add is attack surface - earn its place
Data, configs, permissions - if you can't rewind, you can't recover
Govern vibe coding before it governs you

slides.notes: In this AI vs. AI contest, the side that UNDERSTANDS faster wins. Not the side that deploys more AI. Use GenAI to understand your enterprise deeply enough that neither attackers nor runaway agents have anywhere to hide.
